newsitem.title: USA: W. House's Raines hopes for quick budget progress.
newsitem.headline: W. House's Raines hopes for quick budget progress.

text.p: White House budget director Franklin Raines said he hoped for quick progress in budget talks with congressional Republicans, but warned it could be tough to work out final legislation by the goal of Aug 1.
"We're hopeful we can make progress. On the other hand, there are serious issues," Raines said.
He made his comments as White House officials and Democrats met with congressional Republicans. Republican leaders billed the meeting as an educational session rather than a negotiation.
"There's not much time left until August 1," Raines said.

House and Senate Republicans have been meeting over the past several days to work out coordinated positions on a host of budget issues. The meeting Wednesday was designed to fill the administration in on decisions they had made.
Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici said he hoped to "narrow the issues" so the two sides could more quickly complete negotiations.
Republicans were unable to reach a coordinated position on a Senate plan to raise the federal cigarette tax by 20 cents per pack as well as contentious Medicare issues.
